issue.title: Feature request: opt-in diagnostic SQL statements to purge storage on demand and report lock conflicts
issue.body:
**Emulator version:** v1.5.59 · **Builds on:** #403, #404

### Context

#403 proposes freeing memory from tombstones and old versions, and #404 proposes key-range locking. In test environments it helps to trigger a purge at a known point (end of a test class or shard) rather than on a timer, and to see which tables are causing lock conflicts. Both are easiest to reach from the tools tests already use: any client's `executeQuery`, or `gcloud spanner databases execute-sql`.

### Proposal: `--enable_emulator_diagnostic_statements` (default `false`)

With it off, these statements fail as unknown functions, as today. With it on, `ExecuteSql` and `ExecuteStreamingSql` handle them before any transaction setup:

- **`SELECT EMULATOR_RECLAIM(['Table', ...] [, not_before => ts] [, not_after => ts | not_after_lag => duration] [, delete_rows => bool])`** purges tombstones and versions older than the retention period (optionally only for the named tables and their indexes), then returns the memory to the OS. Result columns: `rows_purged`, `versions_purged`, `rows_deleted` (INT64). `delete_rows => true` deletes live rows written inside a bounded window, which lets a seeded test database drop the test's rows while keeping the seed rows; an unbounded `delete_rows` is rejected. Unknown arguments, unquoted table names and inverted windows are rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
- **`SELECT EMULATOR_LOCK_STATS()`** returns one row per table: `table_name` (STRING), `whole_table_conflicts`, `bounded_conflicts`, `shared_conflicts`, `exclusive_conflicts` (INT64), `last_conflict_time` (TIMESTAMP). Counts are recorded only under key-range locking.

These are test-environment tools: Cloud Spanner has neither statement, and `delete_rows` deletes data. The README documents them under "Optional features", with that warning. Tests cover both RPCs, every argument, every rejection, and the flag-off behaviour. The branch builds and passes `//frontend/handlers/...`, `//backend/storage/...`, `//backend/database/...`, `//backend/locking/...`, `//common/...` and `//gateway/...` on v1.5.59.

Reference branch, on top of the #404 branch with the #403 purge branch merged in: https://github.com/psinghbay1/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/feat/key-range-locking...feat/emulator-diagnostic-statements

We'd understand if a new SQL surface isn't something you want in the emulator; if so, a different trigger for the purge in #403 works for us.

issue.title: "aborted due to concurrent schema change" doesn't say which schema change
issue.body:
**Emulator version:** v1.5.59

When a read-write transaction is aborted because a schema change happened while it was active, the error is:

```
Transaction: <id> aborted due to concurrent schema change.
```

It names neither side, so users can't find the DDL that caused it without server logs, which is hard in CI where many suites apply schema in parallel.

### Proposal

Keep the code `ABORTED` and the existing behaviour (the check still compares schema snapshots exactly as today), and only extend the message:

```
Transaction: <id> aborted due to concurrent schema change. Transaction started on schema version <RFC3339>, latest schema version is <RFC3339> (gap <duration>).
```

The implementation adds `VersionedCatalog::LatestSchemaTime()`, records the creation time of the schema a transaction started on, and passes both to a new overload of `error::AbortDueToConcurrentSchemaChange`. The existing `ConcurrentSchemaUpdatesWithTransactions` test now also checks the message. 39+/2−; builds and passes `//backend/transaction/...`, `//backend/schema/catalog/...` and `//common/...` on v1.5.59.

Reference branch: https://github.com/psinghbay1/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/master...feat/schema-change-abort-detail

Happy for you to take ownership and re-implement it however suits you.

issue.title: Feature request: narrow the locks SQL reads and DML take to the keys they target (builds on #404)
issue.body:
**Emulator version:** v1.5.59 · **Builds on:** #404

### Context

With key-range locking (#404), mutations and key reads lock only the keys they touch, but a SQL read in a read-write transaction still share-locks the whole table, so a SQL-heavy workload still serialises. #390 makes a query *read* only the keys its filters allow, for performance; this is the locking counterpart: the *lock* a SQL read or DML statement takes is narrowed to the same keys.

### Proposal: `--enable_sql_read_pushdown` (default `false`)

Only has an effect with `--enable_key_range_locking`. With it on, these narrow the lock:

- Equality, `IN (...)` and `IN UNNEST(@array)` on leading primary-key columns lock points, or prefixes when only leading columns are pinned (up to 1000 key combinations).
- A range (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `BETWEEN`) on the next key column locks one closed range per prefix, honouring `DESC`.
- With `FORCE_INDEX`, the index range is locked and the base rows found in it get point locks.
- `UPDATE` / `DELETE` use the key filters in their `WHERE`; `INSERT ... VALUES` checks only its own keys; `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` looks up only the inserted conflict-target keys.
- Narrowing applies to key types INT64, STRING, BYTES, BOOL, DATE and TIMESTAMP.

Anything else (non-key filters, no filter, unsupported key types) falls back to today's whole-table lock. With the flag off, the query engine takes exactly today's path.

New unit tests in `backend/query/queryable_table_test.cc` and `query_engine_test.cc` record the key set each scan reads and lock requests, in both modes, plus a conformance case. The branch builds and passes `//backend/query/...`, `//common/...` and `//tests/conformance/cases/...` on v1.5.59.

Reference branch, stacked on the #404 branch: https://github.com/psinghbay1/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/feat/key-range-locking...feat/sql-read-pushdown

Happy for you to take ownership and re-implement it however suits you.

issue.title: Feature request: allow concurrent read-write transactions that touch different keys (opt-in key-range locking)
issue.body:
**Emulator version:** v1.5.59

### Context

The README documents: *"The emulator only allows one read-write transaction or schema change at a time. Any concurrent transaction will be aborted."* For test suites that run in parallel against one emulator, this aborts most concurrent transactions even when they touch unrelated rows, and the random choice of which transaction aborts (`--abort_current_transaction_probability`, default 20) makes retries nondeterministic. Earlier reports: #2, #137, #266; #389 measures related fixed costs.

### Proposal (opt-in)

**1. `--enable_key_range_locking`** (default `false`). Lock by table and key range, in shared or exclusive mode, instead of database-wide. Transactions on disjoint keys proceed and commit concurrently; conflicting transactions still abort with `ABORTED`, so clients keep retrying as today. Schema changes still take a database-wide lock, and commit timestamps stay serialised. `--commit_reservation_wait_ms` bounds how long a committer waits for the commit-timestamp reservation. With the flag off, the lock manager takes upstream's existing code path, abort messages are unchanged, and a second transaction is aborted exactly as today. With it on, abort messages name the overlapping key range and the rule applied.
https://github.com/psinghbay1/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/master...feat/key-range-locking

**2. `--lock_conflict_policy=random|wound_wait`** (default `random`, today's behaviour; only takes effect with `--enable_key_range_locking`). `wound_wait` resolves conflicts deterministically: an older transaction wounds a younger holder, and a younger requester is aborted. Retried transactions keep their original priority, so they eventually win.
https://github.com/psinghbay1/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/feat/key-range-locking...feat/wound-wait (stacked on 1)

Both are forwarded by `gateway_main`, documented in the README under "Optional features", and covered in `backend/locking/manager_test.cc` in both modes (including tests that the defaults keep today's single-transaction behaviour). Each branch builds and passes `//backend/locking/...`, `//common/...` and `//backend/transaction/...` on v1.5.59.

A follow-up that makes this useful for SQL workloads (narrowing the locks a SQL read takes) is filed separately.

Happy to walk through the design, or for you to re-implement it however suits you.

issue.title: Feature request: release memory from deleted rows, idle sessions, finished operations and old schema versions
issue.body:
**Emulator version:** v1.5.59

### Context

CI suites run many write/delete cycles and DDL batches against one long-lived emulator. Several kinds of state are never released during the process lifetime, so memory only grows until the container is restarted:

- **Deleted rows and superseded versions.** A `DELETE` appends a tombstone version; nothing compacts tombstones or versions older than `version_retention_period`.
- **Old schema versions.** Every DDL batch keeps a full copy of the schema (for an hour by default) so old snapshot reads resolve. A CI schema load applies many batches across many databases, then stops.
- **Abandoned sessions and finished long-running operations.** These stay in `SessionManager` / `OperationManager` until deleted explicitly, which test clients that crash or time out never do.

Related: #387 (memory not released after a database is dropped, fixed in v1.5.59), #72, #33.

### Proposal: three independent opt-in flags, all off by default

1. **`--schema_version_retention=<duration>`** (default: keep every version, today's behaviour; `0s` keeps only the latest). A read-only transaction pins the schema version it resolved, so retention never frees a schema that a live transaction uses. A read-write transaction detects a schema change by creation time rather than by pointer, because a freed version's address can be reused. Reads older than the oldest kept schema fail with a clear error.
   https://github.com/psinghbay1/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/master...feat/schema-version-retention
2. **`--session_idle_timeout=<duration>` and `--operation_retention=<duration>`** (default: never prune). Idle sessions are swept on `CreateSession` at most once a minute; multiplexed sessions are never removed. Finished operations are swept on `CreateOperation`, measured from completion; running operations are never removed.
   https://github.com/psinghbay1/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/master...feat/prune-idle-sessions-operations
3. **`--storage_purge_interval=<duration>`** (default: off). A per-database background thread periodically purges tombstones and versions older than the retention period, cleans up dropped tables/columns, then calls `malloc_trim` on glibc. The thread is stopped and joined when the database is destroyed.
   https://github.com/psinghbay1/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/master...feat/purge-tombstones

Each flag is also forwarded by `gateway_main` (with an env var of the same name for `docker run`), documented in the README under "Optional features", and has a test that the unset default keeps today's behaviour. Each branch builds and passes its unit tests on v1.5.59 independently; they touch some of the same files (`common/config`, `gateway.go`, README), so they would need small mechanical merges if taken together.

Happy for you to take ownership and re-implement any of these however suits you.

comments.body:
Thanks for the thorough proposal! Several parts of this have recently been addressed or are already supported:

1. **Returning freed heap pages to the OS & cleaning up Operations**: Fixed in `v1.5.60`, which linked `tcmalloc` (`--custom_malloc=@com_google_tcmalloc//tcmalloc:tcmalloc`) in the Bazel build and cleaned up operations in `OperationManager` when databases, instances, or instance partitions are deleted.
2. **Reclaiming `DROP INDEX` data tables and multiple drops per DDL batch**: We have a fix in review for #400 so `DROP INDEX` marks the index's backing table as dropped.
3. **Controlling `version_retention_period`**: You do not need a new CLI flag to lower the retention window in the emulator—the emulator already allows `version_retention_period` values down to `1s` via standard DDL:
   ```sql
   ALTER DATABASE <db> SET OPTIONS (version_retention_period = '1s')
   ```
   (whereas production Cloud Spanner enforces a 1-hour minimum).

For the remaining two items: sweeping abandoned non multiplexed sessions after the existing 1 hour idle timeout in `SessionManager` (currently evicted lazily in `GetSession`), and compacting delete tombstones in `InMemoryStorage` once they are older than `version_retention_period`; we are evaluating doing this automatically using the existing 1h session TTL and database `version_retention_period` option so no extra CLI flags are required.

issue.title: Conformance test environment never shuts down its gRPC server
issue.body:
**Emulator version:** v1.5.59

`EmulatorConformanceTestEnvironment` (`tests/conformance/endpoints/emulator_conformance_test.cc`) starts a `frontend::Server` in `SetUp()` but never stops it. The gRPC server, with its completion-queue threads and listening port, stays alive until static destruction, after globals it uses have already been destroyed. That can leave threads running and the port bound at exit, and the test process can hang instead of exiting.

### Possible fix

Add `Server::Shutdown(absl::Duration grace)`, which calls `grpc_server_->Shutdown(deadline)` so RPCs still running after the grace period are cancelled, and call it from the environment's `TearDown()` before resetting the server.

Reference implementation (+22 lines) on top of v1.5.59; builds and passes `//frontend/server/...` and `//tests/conformance/endpoints/...`:

https://github.com/psinghbay1/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/master...fix/conformance-server-shutdown

Happy for you to take ownership and re-implement it however suits you.

issue.title: Building from source: CRC32C copts in spanner_pg port, bootstrap_catalog writes into a read-only checkout, Docker build OOM
issue.body:
**Emulator version:** v1.5.59

We hit three problems building the emulator from source. Each has a small, self-contained fix; reference branches on top of v1.5.59 are linked below.

### 1. CRC32C intrinsics in `//third_party/spanner_pg/src/port`

The `port` target compiles the same `pg_crc32c_sse42.c` / `pg_crc32c_armv8.c` sources as `:port_srv`, but without the per-CPU copts `:port_srv` has. The `_mm_crc32_*` / `__crc32*` intrinsics are `always_inline` and need `-msse4.2` (x86_64) or `-march=armv8-a+crc` (aarch64), so the target fails with:

```
inlining failed in call to 'always_inline' ...: target specific option mismatch
```

Fix: the same `select()` on `@platforms//cpu` that `:port_srv` uses.
https://github.com/psinghbay1/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/master...fix/pg-port-crc32c-copts

### 2. `//third_party/spanner_pg/bootstrap_catalog` genrule writes into the source tree

The genrule copies the generated `pg_aggregate.dat` and `pg_proc.dat` over the engine catalog `.dat` files. In the execroot those paths are symlinks into the checkout, so the copy writes through to the sources and fails when the checkout is not writable:

```
cp: cannot create regular file '.../pg_aggregate.dat': Permission denied
```

Fix: copy the `.dat` inputs into a fresh `mktemp -d` directory, make them writable (`cp` preserves Bazel's read-only mode), overlay the generated files with `cp -f`, and use that directory as the catalog path.
https://github.com/psinghbay1/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/master...fix/bootstrap-catalog-readonly-checkout

### 3. `Dockerfile.ubuntu` runs out of memory on smaller hosts

`.bazelrc` sets `--jobs=auto`, which sizes parallelism to the CPU count and ignores memory. GoogleSQL translation units need 1-2 GB each to compile (the bison-generated `tm_parser.cc` can peak at 8-10 GB at -O2), so on a Docker VM with less RAM than cores x 2 GB the image build fails with:

```
gcc: fatal error: Killed signal terminated program cc1plus
```

Fix: two optional build args, empty by default so existing behaviour is unchanged: `BAZEL_JOBS` caps `--jobs`, and `GCC_MEMORY_COPTS` passes extra GCC options (for example `--copt=--param=ggc-min-expand=10`) to both `bazel build` calls. We built and smoke-tested the image both with and without the args.
https://github.com/psinghbay1/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/master...fix/dockerfile-ubuntu

Happy for you to take ownership of any of these and re-implement them however suits you.

issue.title: DROP INDEX leaves the index's data in memory for the life of the process
issue.body:
**Emulator version:** v1.5.59 (also present in v1.5.57 and v1.5.58)

### What happens

After `DROP INDEX`, the rows of the index's backing data table stay in in-memory storage for the life of the emulator process.

In `SchemaUpdater` (`backend/schema/updater/schema_updater.cc`), `DropTable()` and `DropQueue()` add the dropped table's id to `dropped_tables_`, so the storage is told to `MarkDroppedTable()` it and `CleanUpDeletedTables()` later frees its data. `DropIndex()` removes the index from the schema but never adds `index->index_data_table()->id()`, so the index's data is never freed.

### Repro

Create a table with rows, `CREATE INDEX` on it, then `DROP INDEX`. After the version retention period, `CleanUpDeletedTables()` runs but the index data table is still present in `InMemoryStorage`, so a CI suite that creates and drops indexes keeps growing.

### Possible fix

Push the index data table id onto `dropped_tables_` in the `DropIndex` path, as `DropTable` does.

One related detail: `InMemoryStorage` keeps `dropped_tables_` / `dropped_columns_` in a `std::map` keyed by timestamp, and every drop in one schema-change batch shares a timestamp. With the fix alone, `DROP TABLE A; DROP INDEX I` in one batch would overwrite A's entry and leak table A instead. Using `std::multimap` for both keeps every entry.

A reference implementation with tests (a dropped index's data is reclaimed; a table and an index dropped in one batch are both reclaimed; two tables/columns dropped at the same timestamp are both reclaimed) is here, on top of v1.5.59. It builds and passes `//backend/storage/...` and `//backend/schema/updater/...`:

https://github.com/psinghbay1/cloud-spanner-emulator/compare/master...fix/dropindex-frees-index-data

Happy for you to take ownership and re-implement it however suits you.

Related: #387 (the same class of leak for dropped databases, fixed in v1.5.59).

issue.title: Improve performance: DML is analysed twice in QueryEngine::ExecuteSql
issue.body:
`ExecuteSql` always analyses with `prune_unused_columns(true)`. For DML it throws that result away and analyses again with pruning off, even though the kind of statement is known from `IsDMLQuery` before the first analysis.

The suggested fix is to choose the pruning setting from `IsDMLQuery(sql)` up front and skip the second analysis when that guess was right. If it was wrong, the existing second analysis still runs, so behaviour is unchanged. It is a small gain (roughly 5% at 8 clients on a read + update workload in my local measurement) that removes one full analysis per DML statement. The patch is here: https://github.com/mridang/cloud-spanner-emulator/pull/4

issue.title: Improve performance: ExecuteStreamingSql analyses every statement twice, once to check for change streams
issue.body:
Before executing a streaming statement, the handler calls `TryGetChangeStreamMetadata`, which does a full analysis of the SQL just to decide whether it is a change stream query. `ExecuteSql` then analyses the same statement again. After the catalog fix in #396, that first analysis is still about 18% of CPU in a profile of an integration test suite.

Change stream queries must call a table-valued function named `READ_<stream>`, `read_json_<stream>` or `read_proto_bytes_<stream>`, so they all contain `read_` (identifiers are case-insensitive). The suggested fix is to return empty metadata, and skip the extra analysis, when the SQL contains neither `read_` nor a backslash (which could spell it with an escape). Invalid statements still fail, with the same error, from `ExecuteSql`. The patch is here: https://github.com/mridang/cloud-spanner-emulator/pull/3

If you would rather decide this from the resolved statement, or cache the analysis, I am happy to change it. This is the cheapest option I found.

issue.title: Improve performance: ExecuteStreamingSql builds a new FunctionCatalog for every statement
issue.body:
`QueryEngine::TryGetChangeStreamMetadata` is a static function. For every statement that goes through `ExecuteStreamingSql` it creates a new `TypeFactory` and a new `FunctionCatalog`, whose constructor registers the whole set of built-in functions, and then analyses the SQL. It does this only to find out whether the statement is a change stream query, even though the engine already holds a `function_catalog_` and `type_factory_` that `ExecuteSql` uses.

A CPU profile (gperftools, 8 clients each working on their own database) shows `FunctionCatalog::FunctionCatalog` at 67.9% of all samples, and 36.5% of samples in a single atomic add (reference counting) that every thread contends on, so adding clients adds CPU use but little throughput. The profile came from a local `-c opt` build of master at a081a7e with a few unrelated experimental locking changes; the function itself is unchanged upstream.

To reproduce, start the emulator, create 8 databases with `CREATE TABLE t (id INT64 NOT NULL, val STRING(MAX)) PRIMARY KEY(id)`, and run 8 goroutines, one per database, each looping a read-write transaction that does `SELECT val FROM t WHERE id = 0` and then `UPDATE t SET val = @val WHERE id = @id`. Throughput barely grows from 4 to 8 clients while CPU use does.

The fix is to make the function a `const` member that uses the engine's `function_catalog_` and `type_factory_`, as `ExecuteSql` already does (about 10 lines). The patch is here: https://github.com/mridang/cloud-spanner-emulator/pull/2 Related: #389 reports a similar per-statement catalog cost at a different call site.

issue.title: `Update` mutation re-applies DEFAULT to unspecified non-key columns when a primary-key column has DEFAULT or is generated
issue.body:
## Summary

When a table has a primary-key column with a `DEFAULT` expression (e.g. `DEFAULT (GENERATE_UUID())`) or a generated key column, an `Update` **mutation** that does not mention a non-key `DEFAULT` column resets that column to its default value. Cloud Spanner preserves the stored value. The same `UPDATE` via DML preserves it on the emulator too. Tables whose key has no DEFAULT/generated column are not affected.

Emulator: `gcr.io/cloud-spanner-emulator/emulator:latest`, image created 2026-09-15 (v1.5.58). Reproduced with the Node.js client 9.0.0 and with `gcloud` alone (588.0.0), so it is not client-specific.

## Steps to reproduce (gcloud only)

```bash
export SPANNER_EMULATOR_HOST=localhost:9010   # emulator running; gcloud configured for it
gcloud spanner databases create repro --instance=test-instance --ddl="
CREATE TABLE t (
  id     STRING(36) NOT NULL DEFAULT (GENERATE_UUID()),
  status STRING(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT ('draft'),
  n      INT64      NOT NULL DEFAULT (0),
  total  NUMERIC
) PRIMARY KEY (id)"
gcloud spanner databases execute-sql repro --instance=test-instance --sql="INSERT INTO t (id, total) VALUES ('A', 10)"
gcloud spanner databases execute-sql repro --instance=test-instance --sql="UPDATE t SET status = 'sent', n = n + 5 WHERE id = 'A'"
gcloud spanner databases execute-sql repro --instance=test-instance --sql="SELECT id, status, n, total FROM t"
#  A  sent  5  10
gcloud spanner rows update --table=t --database=repro --instance=test-instance --data="id=A,total=11"
gcloud spanner databases execute-sql repro --instance=test-instance --sql="SELECT id, status, n, total FROM t"
#  A  draft  0  11          <-- expected:  A  sent  5  11
```

Same with the Node.js client:

```js
await db.table('t').update([{ id: 'A', total: 11 }]);   // status -> 'draft', n -> 0 on the emulator
```

## Expected

`status = 'sent'`, `n = 5`, `total = 11` — DEFAULT applies to inserts only (Cloud Spanner behaves this way for this exact schema; our suite asserts it against a real instance).

## Observed

`status = 'draft'`, `n = 0`, `total = 11`. Nullable DEFAULT columns are reset too; columns without DEFAULT are preserved.

## What triggers it (bisected, one schema feature at a time)

| Schema | Partial `Update` mutation |
|---|---|
| plain key, no DEFAULT anywhere on the key | preserves |
| + CHECK / secondary index / interleaved child / FK / STORED generated non-key column / commit-timestamp columns | preserves |
| + `DEFAULT (GENERATE_UUID())` on a **non-key** column | preserves |
| **key column with DEFAULT** (`GENERATE_UUID()`, a constant `'k'`, `INT64 DEFAULT (1)`, `UUID DEFAULT (CAST(GENERATE_UUID() AS UUID))`) | **resets other DEFAULT columns** |
| composite key with DEFAULT on only one key column | resets |
| **generated key column** (`k INT64 AS (LENGTH(id)) STORED`), no DEFAULT at all | resets |
| key with DEFAULT, row created by an `Insert` mutation instead of DML | resets |
| key with DEFAULT, partial `UPDATE` by **DML** instead of a mutation | preserves |

## Likely cause

`EvaluatedColumnEffector::Effect(const MutationOp&, …)` (the `for_keys=true` effector that `ActionManager` registers when any key column is generated or has a DEFAULT) iterates the evaluated columns and only skips columns that are *neither key nor DEFAULT*. A non-key DEFAULT column that the mutation does not supply is therefore computed and appended to `evaluated_values` / `columns_with_evaluated_values` regardless of `op.type`; `ReadWriteTransaction::ResolveNonDeleteMutationOp` appends those columns to the mutation, and `FlattenNonDeleteOpRow` turns a `kUpdate` into an `UpdateOp` that now carries the default values as if the client had sent them. The non-key effector (`Effect(const UpdateOp&)`) already has the right rule ("DEFAULT values only apply to inserts"), but the key effector's path bypasses it. Looks like a leftover of the fix for #206.

issue.title: Four fixed costs that dominate test suites on the emulator: clock lead on every read, full-table reads for keyed queries, per-statement catalog rebuild, double analysis of every streaming query (patches available)
issue.body:
We run a 1,500-class Kotlin test suite against the emulator (one container per JVM, a 195-table schema created from a snapshot). Profiling the test JVMs showed over 80% of their time waiting on the emulator, and that most of that time was three fixed costs in the emulator rather than the work the statements do. We fixed them in a fork (a fourth, found afterwards, is section 4 below); each fix is one commit on top of `v1.5.58` (= current `master`) on branch [`upstream-perf`](https://github.com/digitalmirrorai/cloud-spanner-emulator/tree/upstream-perf) of our public fork. The four commits are also open as #390, in case that is the easier way to take them.

### 1. The logical clock runs ahead of the system clock and every read waits for it (#277, likely #159)

`Clock::Now` in `common/clock.cc` adds a microsecond for every call that lands within a microsecond of the previous one and never gives the lead back, and a strong read sleeps in `LockManager::WaitForSafeRead` until the system clock reaches its read timestamp. So every read and query waits the whole accumulated lead: a container that has served a day of test traffic answered a key read in ~42 ms instead of ~1 ms. The fix is the one accepted in #277 (`last = max(last + 1µs, now)`), which is not on `master` yet. [commit](https://github.com/digitalmirrorai/cloud-spanner-emulator/commit/7101f135) with a test.

### 2. A query reads every row of every table it names

`QueryableTable::CreateEvaluatorTableIterator` reads with `KeySet::All()` and leaves the filtering to the evaluator. The evaluator (`push_down_filters` is on in `evaluator_base.cc`) already offers its equality and `IN` filters through `EvaluatorTableIterator::SetColumnFilterMap` before the first row; the iterator ignores them. The patch turns filters on the leading primary-key columns into a key set, so `WHERE tenantId = @t` reads one tenant's rows: a thousand-key `IN UNNEST` lookup over a 5,000-row table went from 20 s to 0.1–0.4 s, and rows left behind by earlier tests stopped taxing every later query. `UPDATE`/`DELETE` are not narrowed (the evaluator does not offer their `WHERE`), and an env var turns the pushdown off. [commit](https://github.com/digitalmirrorai/cloud-spanner-emulator/commit/d24586c2) with tests.

### 3. Every statement rebuilds the query catalog, and that costs 25 ms on a real schema (#187)

`QueryEngine::ExecuteSql` builds a `Catalog` per statement. Building it deep-copied the `AnalyzerOptions` once per table and once per column (passed by value), re-ran the analyzer over every default and generated column expression (59 in our schema), and wrapped the property graph with all its property definitions. `SELECT 1` cost 13 ms idle / 25–35 ms under load against our schema, 1.6 ms against a one-table schema — the schema size was the per-statement price of every query and every DML, which is what #187 measures through default-valued inserts. The patch passes the options by reference, keeps each column expression analysis per query engine (owned by its `FunctionCatalog`, since the resolved tree points at that catalog's functions; expressions over sequences, SQL UDFs or subqueries are never kept), and wraps a property graph on the first statement that names it. `SELECT 1`: 12.9 → 1.1 ms; a keyed `SELECT`: 11.7 → 1.3 ms; a keyed `UPDATE`: 12.2 → 1.3 ms. [commit](https://github.com/digitalmirrorai/cloud-spanner-emulator/commit/0905dc40); `catalog_test`, `query_engine_test`, `queryable_table_test` and `information_schema_catalog_test` pass.

### 4. `ExecuteStreamingSql` analyzes every statement twice

Found after the three above were in place, by benchmarking through the Java client instead of the REST gateway: `SELECT 1` on the same schema and the same emulator process cost 5.4 ms from the Java client and 1.2 ms over REST. The difference is the handler. The REST gateway calls `ExecuteSql`; every client library calls `ExecuteStreamingSql`, and only the streaming handler (`frontend/handlers/queries.cc`) runs `QueryEngine::TryGetChangeStreamMetadata` before `ExecuteSql`. That function builds a fresh `FunctionCatalog` and `Catalog` and analyzes the whole statement — with no column expression cached, so the cost fix 3 removed comes back in full — only to look for a `READ_<stream>` TVF in the resolved tree, after which `ExecuteSql` analyzes the statement again to run it. A change stream query names a `READ_<stream>` (`spanner.read_json_<stream>` / `spanner.read_proto_bytes_<stream>` in the PostgreSQL dialect) of a change stream the schema holds, so the patch returns the empty metadata without analyzing when the schema has no change streams or the statement contains no `read_` at all; every other statement takes the path it always took. `SELECT 1` through the Java client: 5.4 → 0.9 ms; a keyed `SELECT`: 6.3 → 1.2 ms; a key read is 0.35 ms either way. [commit](https://github.com/digitalmirrorai/cloud-spanner-emulator/commit/42cf9e7d) with a test; `query_engine_test` passes. On our suite the time test threads spent inside SQL statements went from 14.6 to 6.3 minutes and the wall clock of a 15,600-test run from 9m00s to 6m43s on the same machine.

### Effect on our suite

Same CI pipeline (each test JVM with its own emulator container), same test code, only the emulator image changed. Only the 583 emulator-backed classes are counted; the pure unit tests are unaffected.

| emulator | emulator-backed tests | summed time of their classes |
|---|---|---|
| upstream 1.5.58 | 5,723 | 166.8 min |
| + fix 1 (#277, #159) and fix 2 | 5,723 | 125.2 min |
| + fix 3 (#187) | 5,741 | 64.7 min |

Not addressed, measured while we were at it: `IN (SELECT …)` and correlated subqueries are evaluated row against row (#209; 1,500 → 6,000 rows took a correlated `EXISTS` from 2 s to 47 s while a `JOIN` on the same predicate stayed at 40 ms), `DELETE` is one transactional delete per row and leaves tombstones scans still walk, and dropping a database returns no memory (#387).

The non-streaming handler never did, which is why benchmarking through the REST gateway hid it. With the first three fixes in place it was the whole difference between `SELECT 1` at 5.4 ms from the Java client and 1.2 ms over REST; skipping it when the schema has no change streams or the statement contains no `read_` brings the Java client to 0.9 ms.

Incorrect INFORMATION_SCHEMA for Cross-Schema Foreign Keys
issue.body:
This appears to be a regression. This bug is preventing me from upgrading from `1.5.33` where this appears to work correctly.

The following is output working with `1.5.54` in the provided docker image.

There are a few bugs around retrieving metadata from the information schema for foreign keys that reference unique indexes across schemas.

## 1. DDL Setup

To reproduce, create a database with the following DDL. It sets up two schemas: a target schema `other_schema` and a default schema. The default schema has tables that reference a unique index in `other_schema`.

```sql
CREATE SCHEMA `other_schema`;

-- Table in non-default schema with a unique index (non-PK target)
CREATE TABLE other_schema.referenced_table (
    id INT64 NOT NULL,
    unique_val INT64 NOT NULL,
) PRIMARY KEY (id);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX other_schema.referenced_table_unique_val_idx
ON other_schema.referenced_table (unique_val);

-- Table in default schema referencing the unique index
CREATE TABLE referring_table (
    id INT64 NOT NULL,
    ref_val INT64 NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT fk_ref_val FOREIGN KEY (ref_val) REFERENCES other_schema.referenced_table (unique_val) NOT ENFORCED
) PRIMARY KEY (id);

-- A second table referencing the same unique index (triggers duplicate rows bug)
CREATE TABLE referring_table_2 (
    id INT64 NOT NULL,
    ref_val INT64 NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT fk_ref_val_2 FOREIGN KEY (ref_val) REFERENCES other_schema.referenced_table (unique_val) NOT ENFORCED
) PRIMARY KEY (id);
```

---

## 2. Demonstrated Bugs in `INFORMATION_SCHEMA`

After creating the tables, query the metadata tables to see the discrepancies.

### Bug A: Mismatch in Constraint Name and Schema
`TABLE_CONSTRAINTS` prefixes the constraint name with the schema and leaves `CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA` empty, while `REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS` does not.

```sql
-- Query RC
SELECT constraint_name, unique_constraint_schema, unique_constraint_name 
FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS 
WHERE constraint_name = 'fk_ref_val';
```
**Output:**
```
+-----------------+--------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------+
| constraint_name | unique_constraint_schema | unique_constraint_name                                  |
+-----------------+--------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------+
| fk_ref_val      | other_schema             | IDX_referenced_table_unique_val_U_6279FBB6083F67DA      |
+-----------------+--------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------+
```

```sql
-- Query TC
SELECT constraint_schema, constraint_name, table_schema, table_name, constraint_type 
FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLE_CONSTRAINTS 
WHERE table_name = 'referenced_table' AND constraint_type = 'UNIQUE';
```
**Output:**
```
+-------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------+------------------+-----------------+
| constraint_schema | constraint_name                                                         | table_schema | table_name       | constraint_type |
+-------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------+------------------+-----------------+
|                   | other_schema.IDX_referenced_table_unique_val_U_6279FBB6083F67DA         | other_schema | referenced_table | UNIQUE          |
|                   | other_schema.IDX_referenced_table_unique_val_U_6279FBB6083F67DA         | other_schema | referenced_table | UNIQUE          |
+-------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------+------------------+-----------------+
```

**Discrepancies:**
*   `TABLE_CONSTRAINTS.CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA` is **empty string `''`** instead of `'other_schema'`.
*   `TABLE_CONSTRAINTS.CONSTRAINT_NAME` is **`other_schema.IDX_...`** (prefixed) but `REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS.UNIQUE_CONSTRAINT_NAME` is **`IDX_...`** (unprefixed).
*   `TABLE_CONSTRAINTS` contains **duplicate identical rows** (see Bug C).

---

### Bug B: Mismatch in `KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` Schema
`KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` also leaves the `CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA` empty for unique indexes.

```sql
SELECT constraint_schema, constraint_name, table_schema, table_name, column_name 
FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE 
WHERE table_name = 'referenced_table' AND constraint_name LIKE 'IDX_%';
```
**Output:**
```
+-------------------+----------------------------------------------------+--------------+------------------+-------------+
| constraint_schema | constraint_name                                    | table_schema | table_name       | column_name |
+-------------------+----------------------------------------------------+--------------+------------------+-------------+
|                   | IDX_referenced_table_unique_val_U_6279FBB6083F67DA | other_schema | referenced_table | unique_val  |
|                   | IDX_referenced_table_unique_val_U_6279FBB6083F67DA | other_schema | referenced_table | unique_val  |
+-------------------+----------------------------------------------------+--------------+------------------+-------------+
```
**Discrepancy:**
*   `KEY_COLUMN_USAGE.CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA` is **empty string `''`** instead of `'other_schema'`.

---

### Bug C: Duplicate Rows
Having multiple foreign keys referencing the same unique index causes the emulator to duplicate the index representation in `TABLE_CONSTRAINTS` and `KEY_COLUMN_USAGE`.

In the outputs above for **Bug A** and **Bug B**, notice that there are **two identical rows** returned for the unique index. This is because both `referring_table` and `referring_table_2` reference it. Adding more referencing tables increases the duplication.

---

## 3. Impact on Standard Joins

SQLAlchemy (and other tools) reflects foreign keys by joining these tables on catalog, schema, and name:

```sql
SELECT rc.constraint_name, tc_uq.table_name
FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS AS rc
JOIN INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLE_CONSTRAINTS AS tc_uq
  ON tc_uq.constraint_catalog = rc.unique_constraint_catalog
  AND tc_uq.constraint_schema = rc.unique_constraint_schema
  AND tc_uq.constraint_name = rc.unique_constraint_name
WHERE rc.constraint_name = 'fk_ref_val';
```

In the emulator, this query returns **`0` rows** (instead of `1`), because:
*   `tc_uq.constraint_schema` (`''`) != `rc.unique_constraint_schema` (`'other_schema'`)
*   `tc_uq.constraint_name` (`'other_schema.IDX_...'`) != `rc.unique_constraint_name` (`'IDX_...'`)

issue.title: ALTER CHANGE STREAM ... SET FOR leaves a column-tracked table tracked, blocking DROP TABLE (1.5.54)
issue.body:
## Summary

Removing a **column-tracked** table (`FOR T(col)`) from a change stream's `FOR` clause via `ALTER CHANGE STREAM ... SET FOR` updates `information_schema` correctly (the table no longer shows as tracked), but does **not** clear the table's internal explicit-tracking back-reference. A subsequent `DROP TABLE` is then wrongly rejected:

> Cannot drop table Z. Table Z is tracked by 1 Change Stream: CS. Tables explicitly tracked by a Change Stream cannot be dropped...

Whole-table tracking (`FOR T`) is unaffected, and `DROP CHANGE STREAM` clears tracking correctly — so the bug is specific to **untracking a column-tracked table via `SET FOR`**. It blocks normal schema evolution: a table that was ever column-tracked by a change stream can't be dropped, even after it's removed from the `FOR` clause. (Distinct from the now-fixed false per-column-limit bug, #298.)

## Environment

- `gcr.io/cloud-spanner-emulator/emulator:1.5.54` (latest; reproduced)
- Still present on current `main` by source inspection — see *Root cause*.

## Minimal repro

```bash
docker run -d --rm --name emu -p 9010:9010 -p 9020:9020 gcr.io/cloud-spanner-emulator/emulator:1.5.54
gcloud config configurations create emu --no-activate
gcloud config set --configuration=emu auth/disable_credentials true
gcloud config set --configuration=emu project test-project
gcloud config set --configuration=emu api_endpoint_overrides/spanner http://localhost:9020/
gcloud config configurations activate emu
gcloud spanner instances create test-instance --config=emulator-config --nodes=1

gcloud spanner databases create db --instance=test-instance \
  --ddl='CREATE TABLE K (Id INT64, c INT64) PRIMARY KEY(Id)' \
  --ddl='CREATE TABLE Z (Id INT64, c INT64) PRIMARY KEY(Id)' \
  --ddl='CREATE CHANGE STREAM CS FOR K(c), Z(c)'

# Remove Z from the change stream's FOR clause:
gcloud spanner databases ddl update db --instance=test-instance \
  --ddl='ALTER CHANGE STREAM CS SET FOR K(c)'

# information_schema confirms CS now tracks only K:
gcloud spanner databases execute-sql db --instance=test-instance \
  --sql="SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.change_stream_tables WHERE change_stream_name='CS'"
# -> K   (Z is gone)

# ...but dropping Z fails:
gcloud spanner databases ddl update db --instance=test-instance --ddl='DROP TABLE Z'
```

**Expected:** `DROP TABLE Z` succeeds — Z is no longer in `CS`'s `FOR` clause.

**Actual:**
```
ERROR: ... Cannot drop table Z. Table Z is tracked by 1 Change Stream: CS.
Tables explicitly tracked by a Change Stream cannot be dropped. Please drop the
Change Stream or modify its FOR clause to stop tracking the table explicitly
before dropping the table.
```

### Controls (isolate the trigger)

- **Whole-table tracking works:** `CREATE CHANGE STREAM CS FOR K, Z` → `ALTER CHANGE STREAM CS SET FOR K` → `DROP TABLE Z` **succeeds**.
- **`DROP CHANGE STREAM` works:** `CREATE CHANGE STREAM CS FOR Z(c)` → `DROP CHANGE STREAM CS` → `DROP TABLE Z` **succeeds**.

Only removing a *column-tracked* table from the `FOR` clause via `SET FOR` triggers it.

## Root cause

In `backend/schema/updater/schema_updater.cc`, `RegisterTrackedObjects` records explicit table tracking **asymmetrically**:

- it always adds the table to `change_streams_explicitly_tracking_table_`;
- it adds the table to the table's general `change_streams_` list **only** in the `has_all_columns()` (whole-table) branch — not in the `has_tracked_columns()` (column-only) branch.

`UnregisterChangeStreamFromTrackedObjects` guards the table cleanup on `Table::FindChangeStream`, which searches **only** the general `change_streams_` list:

```cpp
const Table* table = latest_schema_->FindTable(table_name);
if (table->FindChangeStream(change_stream->Name())) {   // false for a column-only tracked table
  GOOGLESQL_RETURN_IF_ERROR(AlterNode(table, table_cb)); // remove_change_stream -> also clears explicit list
}
```

For a column-only tracked table the guard is false, so `change_streams_explicitly_tracking_table_` is never cleared — and the `DROP TABLE` validation, which reads that list, keeps failing.

## Suggested fix

Always run the table-unregister callback. `Table::Editor::remove_change_stream` is idempotent (both erases are guarded by `if (itr != end())`), so it's safe when the stream isn't in the general list:

```diff
   const Table* table = latest_schema_->FindTable(table_name);
-  if (table->FindChangeStream(change_stream->Name())) {
-    GOOGLESQL_RETURN_IF_ERROR(AlterNode(table, table_cb));
-  }
+  GOOGLESQL_RETURN_IF_ERROR(AlterNode(table, table_cb));
```

A reference fix — this one-line change plus a conformance regression test in `tests/conformance/data/schema_changes/change_streams.test` — is on a fork for convenience:
https://github.com/darryljjennings/cloud-spanner-emulator/commit/9b2632fd

(I see CONTRIBUTING.md notes external code contributions aren't currently accepted — this is just for reference/repro; happy to provide it in whatever form is most useful.)

issue.title: Change-stream mods.keys JSON drops sub-second precision for TIMESTAMP columns
issue.body:
When a tracked table has a `TIMESTAMP` column in its primary key, the change-stream `DataChangeRecord.mods[].keys` JSON encodes that column without fractional seconds. Real Spanner preserves up to 9 fractional digits.

Repro:
1. CREATE TABLE t (commit_ts TIMESTAMP NOT NULL, k INT64) PRIMARY KEY (commit_ts, k) + CREATE CHANGE STREAM s FOR t
2. Insert a row with commit_ts = TIMESTAMP '1970-01-21T14:09:51.234567890Z'
3. Read the change-stream; mods[0].keys.commit_ts is "1970-01-21T14:09:51Z" (decimals dropped)

Cause: [backend/actions/change_stream.cc CloudValueToJSONValue](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/29ac12f2bb17cead8ca06a5db6b1bb4e5bf0d8d3/backend/actions/change_stream.cc#L565) uses `absl::FormatTime("%Y-%m-%d%ET%H:%M:%SZ", ...)` for `TYPE_TIMESTAMP` — `%S` emits integer seconds. Real Spanner emits fractional. The fix is `%E*S` (or `%E9S`).

Same function as #328 (UUID encoding), similar shape of fix.

Affected: any consumer that reconstructs row identity from keys JSON when a TIMESTAMP is part of the PK.

issue.title: DEFAULT (PENDING_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP()) fails with FailedPrecondition when table has a generated stored primary key.
issue.body:
When a table combines a generated stored column as the primary key (e.g. extracted from a JSON column via JSON_VALUE) with DEFAULT (PENDING_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP()) / ON UPDATE (PENDING_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP()) timestamp columns, both DML and Mutation API inserts fail with:
`FailedPrecondition: Cannot write timestamps in the future, found: 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999999+00:00`
**Steps to reproduce**

1. Start the emulator and create an instance/database
2. Create a table with a generated stored PK + default commit timestamps:
```
CREATE TABLE TestTable (
    test_id STRING(100) AS (JSON_VALUE(data, '$.test_id')) STORED,
    data JSON,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT (PENDING_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP()) OPTIONS (allow_commit_timestamp = true),
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT (PENDING_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP()) ON UPDATE (PENDING_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP()) OPTIONS (allow_commit_timestamp = true),
) PRIMARY KEY (test_id)
```
3. Insert a row via DML:
```
INSERT INTO TestTable (data) VALUES (JSON '{"test_id": "dml-1", "name": "DML Insert"}')
```
4. Insert a row via Mutation API (Go example):
```
client.Apply(ctx, []*spanner.Mutation{
    spanner.InsertMap("TestTable", map[string]interface{}{
        "data": spanner.NullJSON{Value: map[string]interface{}{
            "test_id": "mutation-1",
            "name":    "Mutation API Insert",
        }, Valid: true},
    }),
})
```

**Expected behavior**
Both inserts succeed. The emulator resolves PENDING_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP() defaults to the actual commit timestamp, as it does for tables without generated stored primary keys.

**Actual behavior**
Both inserts fail with:
`spanner: code = "FailedPrecondition", desc = "Cannot write timestamps in the future, found: 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999999+00:00"
`

**Environment**
- Emulator image: gcr.io/cloud-spanner-emulator/emulator (v1.5.48)
- Client: cloud.google.com/go/spanner v1.87.0

**Reproduction repo**
https://github.com/jmbradshaw79/spanner-emulator-generated-key-bug

**Note:** 
- This bug also occurs sourcing from a proto column field, which is my actual use case. 
- This bug does not occur in cloud spanner

Feature Request: Support local embedding services for ML.PREDICT testing

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Feature Request: Local Embedding Service Support for ML.PREDICT

### Problem Statement

The Cloud Spanner Emulator currently generates single-element fingerprint hashes for ML.PREDICT instead of real embeddings. This causes validation failures when testing vector similarity search locally:

```
INVALID_ARGUMENT: Array column embeddings has 1 elements and is less than
the `vector_length` limit: 1024
```

Developers cannot effectively test ML.PREDICT and vector search features locally without connecting to external cloud services (Vertex AI, OpenAI), which requires:
- Network connectivity and API keys
- API costs for every test run
- Slower iteration cycles

### Proposed Solution

Add support for local/self-hosted embedding services in the emulator via a `local://` endpoint prefix convention:

```sql
CREATE MODEL text_embeddings
INPUT (content STRING(MAX))
OUTPUT (embedding ARRAY<FLOAT32>(vector_length=>1024))
REMOTE OPTIONS (
  endpoint = 'local://localhost:8080/embed'  -- Points to local service
);
```

When the emulator detects a `local://` endpoint, it would:
1. Make HTTP POST request to the local service with input text
2. Parse the embedding vector response
3. Return properly formatted ARRAY<FLOAT32> with correct dimensions
4. Validate dimensions match `vector_length` constraints

### Use Cases

**Development & Testing:**
- Test vector similarity search end-to-end without cloud dependencies
- Validate schema constraints (vector_length, distance functions, indexes)
- Run automated tests in CI/CD pipelines offline

**Model Flexibility:**
- Use open-source models (Sentence-Transformers, Qwen, BGE, etc.)
- Test custom fine-tuned embedding models
- Evaluate different embedding dimensions before production deployment

**Cost & Speed:**
- Zero API costs during development
- Faster iteration (no network latency to cloud services)
- Work offline or in restricted network environments

### Example Workflow

```sql
-- 1. Drop and recreate table with FLOAT64
CREATE TABLE documents (
  doc_id STRING(MAX),
  content STRING(MAX),
  embedding ARRAY<FLOAT64>(vector_length=>1024)
) PRIMARY KEY (doc_id);

-- 2. Create model with FLOAT64 output
CREATE MODEL local_embeddings1
  INPUT (content STRING(MAX))
  OUTPUT (embedding ARRAY<FLOAT64>(vector_length=>1024))
  REMOTE OPTIONS (endpoint = 'local://localhost:8080/embed'
);

-- 3. Now the INSERT should work
INSERT INTO documents (doc_id, content, embedding)
SELECT doc_id, content, embedding
FROM ML.PREDICT(MODEL local_embeddings1, (
    SELECT "doc1" as doc_id, "Cloud Spanner is great" as content
));
```

### Benefits

1. **Improved Developer Experience**: Complete local testing of vector search features
2. **Cost Savings**: No API charges during development/testing phases
3. **Faster Development**: Immediate feedback without network round-trips
4. **CI/CD Integration**: Automated tests can run without external service dependencies
5. **Model Experimentation**: Easy comparison of different embedding models/dimensions
6. **Broader Adoption**: Lowers barrier to entry for vector search development

### Technical Considerations

**Protocol Compatibility:**
Support common embedding service APIs (HuggingFace Text Embeddings Inference, Ollama, etc.):
```json
Request:  {"inputs": "text content", "truncate": true}
Response: [[0.334, -0.123, 0.456, ...]]
```

**Backward Compatibility:**
- Existing fingerprint-based behavior remains default
- Only activates with explicit `local://` endpoint
- No breaking changes to query engine or storage layer
- Works with both GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL dialects

### Implementation Reference

A working proof-of-concept implementation is available demonstrating the approach:
- Endpoint detection and routing in ModelEvaluator
- HTTP client for local service communication
- Configuration system and error handling
- Integration with existing ML.PREDICT architecture

Repository: https://github.com/nordanster/cloud-spanner-emulator/tree/feature/local-embeddings

Key changes:
- `backend/query/ml/model_evaluator.{h,cc}` - Endpoint routing logic
- `backend/query/ml/embedding_client.{h,cc}` - HTTP client (new)
- `common/config.{h,cc}` - Configuration flags
- `WORKSPACE` - HTTP library dependency (cpp-httplib)

### Community Impact

This feature would significantly benefit:
- **RAG Application Developers**: Building retrieval-augmented generation systems
- **ML Engineers**: Testing embedding models before production deployment
- **Enterprise Teams**: Using self-hosted models for data privacy/compliance
- **Educational Content**: Tutorials and workshops on Cloud Spanner vector search
- **Open Source Community**: Developers using local/open-source embedding models

### Priority Rationale

Vector embeddings and similarity search are increasingly important for AI/ML workloads. As Cloud Spanner's vector search capabilities mature, enabling effective local development becomes critical for adoption.

Currently, developers must choose between:
1. Testing with fake data (fingerprint hashes) that fail validation
2. Connecting to expensive cloud services for every test
3. Not testing locally at all

This feature eliminates that trade-off and aligns the emulator with modern AI development workflows.

---

**Additional Context:**
- Vector search is a key differentiator for Cloud Spanner in AI workloads
- Local embedding services are standard practice (Ollama, HuggingFace TEI, etc.)
- Similar pattern already exists for PostgreSQL dialect (PgPredict with local endpoints)
- No changes required to production Cloud Spanner (emulator-only feature)

Thank you for considering this feature request!

It is useful to ensure that the query is valid, but sometimes, valid queries can be rejected because of unimplemented hints.

Ideally, all valid queries with hints should be accepted.

[Statement Hints](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/query-syntax#statement_hints)

|`OPTIMIZER_VERSION`|No|
|`OPTIMIZER_STATISTICS_PACKAGE`|No|
|`ALLOW_DISTRIBUTED_MERGE`|No|
|`LOCK_SCANNED_RANGES	`|Yes|

issue.title: Change stream ALTER operations incorrectly accumulate internal state causing false limit violations
issue.body:
The Spanner emulator enforces a limit that "no more than 3 change streams can track the same non-key column" (as documented in the [quotas page](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/quotas)). However, when a change stream undergoes multiple `ALTER CHANGE STREAM` operations, the emulator appears to accumulate internal state incorrectly, causing false violations of this limit.

Specifically, after performing multiple ALTER operations on a change stream that tracks a column (e.g., `numericId`) in 3 tables, subsequent attempts to add additional tables to the change stream fail with a "more than 3 Change Streams" error, even when:
1. There is still only ONE change stream in the database
2. The new table being added does NOT contain the restricted column

**Environment:**
- Emulator version: 1.5.28 (tested via `gcr.io/cloud-spanner-emulator/emulator:1.5.28`)
- Testing method: Docker container + gcloud CLI

**Expected Behavior:**

According to the [Spanner quotas documentation](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/quotas), the limit is:
> **Change streams watching any given non-key column: 3**

This means up to **3 separate change streams** can track the same column. A single change stream tracking a column in multiple tables should count as **1 change stream** watching that column, regardless of how many ALTER operations have been performed on it.

**Actual Behavior:**

After performing multiple `ALTER CHANGE STREAM` operations on a change stream that tracks `numericId` in 3 tables, attempting to add a 4th table (even one without `numericId`) fails with:

```
ERROR: (gcloud.spanner.databases.ddl.update) HTTPError 400: {"code":9, "message":"Failed to create or alter Change Stream S : because it is not allowed to have more than 3 Change Streams tracking the same table or non-key column or ALL: numericId."}
```

**Root Cause Analysis:**

The bug appears to be that each `ALTER CHANGE STREAM` operation creates new internal state tracking the column usage, but doesn't properly clean up the old state. After multiple ALTERs, the emulator incorrectly believes the limit has been reached.

**Minimal Reproduction Steps:**

1. Start the Spanner emulator:
```bash
docker run -d --rm --name spanner-emulator -p 9010:9010 -p 9020:9020 gcr.io/cloud-spanner-emulator/emulator:1.5.28
```

2. Configure gcloud to use the emulator:
```bash
gcloud config configurations create emulator --no-activate
gcloud config set --configuration=emulator auth/disable_credentials true
gcloud config set --configuration=emulator project local-project
echo "y" | gcloud config set --configuration=emulator api_endpoint_overrides/spanner http://localhost:9020/
gcloud config configurations activate emulator
```

3. Create instance and database:
```bash
gcloud spanner instances create local-instance --config=emulator-config --description="Local Instance" --nodes=1
gcloud spanner databases create local-database --instance=local-instance
```

4. Create 3 tables with `numericId` column and 1 table without it:
```bash
gcloud spanner databases ddl update local-database --instance=local-instance --ddl="CREATE TABLE T1 (id STRING(36) NOT NULL, numericId INT64 NOT NULL, col1 STRING(MAX), col2 STRING(MAX)) PRIMARY KEY (id)"

gcloud spanner databases ddl update local-database --instance=local-instance --ddl="CREATE TABLE T2 (id STRING(36) NOT NULL, numericId INT64 NOT NULL, col1 STRING(MAX), col2 STRING(MAX)) PRIMARY KEY (id)"

gcloud spanner databases ddl update local-database --instance=local-instance --ddl="CREATE TABLE T3 (id STRING(36) NOT NULL, numericId INT64 NOT NULL, col1 STRING(MAX), col2 STRING(MAX)) PRIMARY KEY (id)"

gcloud spanner databases ddl update local-database --instance=local-instance --ddl="CREATE TABLE T4 (id STRING(36) NOT NULL, status STRING(MAX)) PRIMARY KEY (id)"
```

5. Create a change stream tracking `numericId` in 3 tables:
```bash
gcloud spanner databases ddl update local-database --instance=local-instance --ddl="CREATE CHANGE STREAM S FOR T1(numericId, col1), T2(numericId, col1), T3(numericId, col1) OPTIONS (value_capture_type = 'NEW_ROW')"
```

6. Verify there is only ONE change stream:
```bash
gcloud spanner databases execute-sql local-database --instance=local-instance --sql="SELECT CHANGE_STREAM_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.CHANGE_STREAMS"
```

**Expected output:** Only `S`

7. Perform multiple ALTER operations on the change stream (modifying which columns are tracked):

```bash
# ALTER #1 - add col2 to all tables
gcloud spanner databases ddl update local-database --instance=local-instance --ddl="ALTER CHANGE STREAM S SET FOR T1(numericId, col1, col2), T2(numericId, col1, col2), T3(numericId, col1, col2)"

# ALTER #2 - remove col2 from all tables
gcloud spanner databases ddl update local-database --instance=local-instance --ddl="ALTER CHANGE STREAM S SET FOR T1(numericId, col1), T2(numericId, col1), T3(numericId, col1)"

# ALTER #3 - add col2 back to all tables
gcloud spanner databases ddl update local-database --instance=local-instance --ddl="ALTER CHANGE STREAM S SET FOR T1(numericId, col1, col2), T2(numericId, col1, col2), T3(numericId, col1, col2)"

# ALTER #4 - remove col2 again
gcloud spanner databases ddl update local-database --instance=local-instance --ddl="ALTER CHANGE STREAM S SET FOR T1(numericId, col1), T2(numericId, col1), T3(numericId, col1)"
```

All 4 ALTER operations should succeed.

8. Now attempt to add T4 (which does NOT have `numericId`) to the change stream:

```bash
gcloud spanner databases ddl update local-database --instance=local-instance --ddl="ALTER CHANGE STREAM S SET FOR T1(numericId, col1), T2(numericId, col1), T3(numericId, col1), T4(status)"
```

**Expected:** Should succeed because:
- There is still only 1 change stream in the database
- T4 does not contain the `numericId` column
- We should be able to have up to 3 change streams tracking `numericId`

**Actual:** Fails with:
```
ERROR: (gcloud.spanner.databases.ddl.update) HTTPError 400: {"code":9, "message":"Failed to create or alter Change Stream S : because it is not allowed to have more than 3 Change Streams tracking the same table or non-key column or ALL: numericId."}
```

9. Verify there is still only ONE change stream:
```bash
gcloud spanner databases execute-sql local-database --instance=local-instance --sql="SELECT CHANGE_STREAM_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.CHANGE_STREAMS"
```

**Output:** Still only `S`

**Cleanup:**
```bash
docker rm -f spanner-emulator
gcloud config configurations activate default
```

**Key Observations:**

1. If you skip steps 7 (the multiple ALTERs) and go directly from step 6 to step 8, the operation **succeeds**
2. The bug is specifically triggered by performing multiple ALTER operations before attempting to add a new table
3. The number of ALTER operations needed to trigger the bug appears to be around 4
4. Each ALTER operation seems to create internal state that incorrectly accumulates toward the limit

**Analysis:**

The quota limit states "3 change streams watching any given non-key column". The emulator should be counting:
- ✅ Number of distinct CHANGE STREAM objects tracking `numericId`: 1

But instead appears to be counting something like:
- ❌ Number of ALTER operations performed × number of tables tracking `numericId`: 4 ALTERs × 3 tables = 12 (or similar accumulation)

This suggests that `ALTER CHANGE STREAM` operations are not properly cleaning up or replacing the old internal state, but instead accumulating new state that incorrectly counts toward the limit.

**Impact:**

This bug prevents normal schema evolution patterns for change streams. In production use cases, change streams often need to be modified over time to add/remove columns or tables. After several such modifications, users hit this artificial limit even though they have not violated the actual documented quota.

issue.title: Emulator doesn't recreate unsupported query shape that can return a null-valued array of struct
issue.body:
Consider the following query that works on spanner emulator, but doesn't work on prod spanner:

```sql
with
  grps as (select * from unnest([10, 20, 30]) as group_id),
  nums as (select * from
    unnest(array<struct<id int64, group_id int64, name string>>[
      (1, 10, 'foo'), (2, 20, 'bar'), (11, 10, 'baz')
    ])
  ) 

select group_id, (select array_agg(struct(id, name)) from nums where nums.group_id=grps.group_id) from grps;
```

Prod spanner reports:

`ERROR: spanner: code="Unimplemented", desc: Unsupported query shape: This query can return a null-valued array of struct, which is not supported by Spanner. ARRAY<STRUCT<id INT64, name STRING>> is the type that might contain null values. Use IFNULL/COALESCE to convert potentially null values to non-null values.`

While in the emulator, this query succeeds.

<hr>

Note that to fix on prod, we follow the error message's advise to use `ifnull/coalesce`:

```sql
with
  grps as (select * from unnest([10, 20, 30]) as group_id),
  nums as (select * from
    unnest(array<struct<id int64, group_id int64, name string>>[
      (1, 10, 'foo'), (2, 20, 'bar'), (11, 10, 'baz')
    ])
  ) 

select group_id, (select coalesce(array_agg(struct(id, name)), []) from nums where nums.group_id=grps.group_id) from grps;
```

However, on the emulator, this fails due to the related issue #165.

issue.title: Request: recovery method when a commit aborts at the RPC level
issue.body:
Request for enhanced concurrent transaction handling in Cloud Spanner Emulator to support testing scenarios with gRPC interceptor-based fault injection.

## Background

We are migrating our unit tests from production Spanner to Spanner Emulator. Our existing tests use an internal fault injection library that intercepts gRPC calls at the client level to verify proper handling of Abort errors.

## Current Problem

The emulator's current constraint ([README](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/master/README.md#features-and-limitations)):
> The emulator only allows one read-write transaction or schema change at a time. Any concurrent transaction will be aborted.

When our fault injection tool returns an Abort error **before** the actual Commit RPC reaches the emulator:
1. The RPC never reaches the emulator
2. The original transaction remains open in the emulator (not committed/rolled back)
3. Retry attempts cannot start new transactions due to the "one RW transaction at a time" constraint
4. Tests fail regardless of correct retry implementation

## Current Workaround

Use `--enable_fault_injection` option instead.
However, there are some complaints.

- **Non-deterministic**: Cannot reliably reproduce specific failure scenarios
- **Development workflow**: Difficult to debug retry logic

We would prefer to maintain our current approach if possible.

## IMHO

I'm not familiar with the inner mechanics of Spanner Emulator, but I think it would be nice if it had a mode like this.

Last-Tx-Wins Mode (current behavior is First-Tx-Win Mode)
Add an option (e.g., `--transaction_last_wins`).
New RW transactions automatically abort/rollback previous uncommitted transactions.

Of course, other methods are fine too, and it would be even better if it behaved exactly like the real Spanner.

**Version:** 1.5.37

**Description:**
When testing our app against the Spanner Graph Emulator, we encountered two limitations that differ from behavior in production Spanner Graph:

issue.title: Linux binary dynamically links too new a version of libstdc++
issue.body:
It appears that the libstdc++ dependency version was upgraded. This version is too new for Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 12 (stable), where the latest package is from GCC 12. This results in the error "version `GLIBCXX_3.4.32' not found" when attempting to run the emulator.

> tested on Ubuntu 18.04+, CentOS 7+, RHEL 8+ and Debian 10+

and

> Production releases of the emulator are built on Ubuntu 18.04 with bazel 5.4.0 and gcc 8.4

This is particularly troublesome as it means the prebuilt binary will no longer run on [Distroless](https://github.com/GoogleContainerTools/distroless), which is based on Debian stable.

2. The grpc dep needs to be updated to 1.65 to pick up https://github.com/grpc/grpc/commit/e55f69cedd0ef7344e0bcb64b5ec9205e6aa4f04

I managed to get this to work on Ubuntu 22.04 with Clang 15. See [my fork](https://github.com/SanjayVas/cloud-spanner-emulator).

Note that it looks like emulator_main was intended to be statically linked to the standard C++ library, as it has `-static-libstdc++` in its `linkopts`. Of course, that's not sufficient for Bazel since it builds using `gcc`/`clang` by default instead of `g++`/`clang++`.

I *believe* the correct approach is to create a `cc_toolchain` that specifies the standard library in [static_runtime_lib](https://bazel.build/reference/be/c-cpp#cc_toolchain.static_runtime_lib) and then use the `static_link_cpp_runtimes` feature.

issue.title: FORCE_INDEX=PRIMARY_KEY not supported by emulator
issue.body:
### Reproduce:
Create a query which contains `FROM MyTable@{FORCE_INDEX=PRIMARY_KEY}` statement

### Expected behaviour:
Query is executed (as it is using a regular Spanner instance)

### Actual outcome:
The following error is returned:
`com.google.cloud.spanner.SpannerException, with message: INVALID_ARGUMENT: io.grpc.StatusRuntimeException: INVALID_ARGUMENT: The table  does not have a secondary index called PRIMARY_KEY`

comments.body:
(Reference: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/secondary-indexes?hl=en#index-directive)

`FORCE_INDEX=_BASE_TABLE` is documented as a way to force a base table scan, but `FORCE_INDEX=PRIMARY_KEY` is not.
Given that `PRIMARY_KEY` being used internally as a pseudo-index name is an implementation detail, and we shouldn't depend on undocumented behavior, perhaps it's acceptable for the emulator to continue rejecting `FORCE_INDEX=PRIMARY_KEY`.
(However, providing a clearer error message would be beneficial.)

issue.title: Timestamps reported in change records values are incorrect
issue.body:
We're using change streams to observe changes to a table, which has two `TIMESTAMP` columns: `resource_version` and `previous_resource_version`.

`resource_version` is always updated with `PENDING_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP()` (which has [microseconds precision](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/commit-timestamp#:~:text=Spanner%20commit%20timestamps%20have%20microsecond%20granularity%2Cand%20they%20are%20converted%20to%20nanoseconds%20when%20stored%20in%20TIMESTAMP%20columns.)), while `previous_resource_version` is updated with computed value.

After modifying the entry we can see following values in the table:

```
+--------------+----------------------------+-----------------------------+
| value        | resource_version           | previous_resource_version   |
+--------------+----------------------------+-----------------------------+
| bmV3LXZhbHVl | 2025-02-19T13:55:36.43168Z | 2025-02-19T13:55:36.429694Z |
+--------------+----------------------------+-----------------------------+
```

However change record with this modification contains following "NEW" values:

```json
{
    "previous_resource_version": "2025-02-19T13:55:36Z",
    "resource_version": "9999-12-31T23:59:59Z",
    "value": "bmV3LXZhbHVl"
}
```

There are two problems with this change record modification:
* `resource_version` column seem to contain placeholder value, instead of final value of `PENDING_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP()`.
* Both `resource_version` and `previous_resource_version` are reported with seconds precision, [instead of nanoseconds](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types#timestamp_type).

When running the same code against cloud Spanner instance, we're seeing correct values in the change record (i.e. final value of commit timestamp and timestamps with microseconds).

Interleaved search index incorrectly requires parent key in token_column_list
issue.body:
Interleaved search indexes incorrectly require the parent key in the `token_column_list` parameter.

```sql
CREATE TABLE one (
  one_id STRING(MAX) NOT NULL
)
PRIMARY KEY (one_id);

CREATE TABLE two (
  one_id       STRING(MAX) NOT NULL,
  two_id       STRING(MAX) NOT NULL,
  title        STRING(MAX),
  title_tokens TOKENLIST AS (TOKENIZE_SUBSTRING(title)) HIDDEN
)
PRIMARY KEY (one_id, two_id),
INTERLEAVE IN PARENT one;
```

Creating the valid search index fails:

```sql
CREATE SEARCH INDEX search_title ON two (title_tokens)
  PARTITION BY one_id,
  INTERLEAVE IN one
  OPTIONS (sort_order_sharding = true);
```

With the following error:

```
code = FailedPrecondition desc = Index search_title does not reference index parent key column one_id.
```

You can work around this in the emulator by adding the column, but this won't work in Google Cloud:

```sql
CREATE SEARCH INDEX search_title ON two (one_id, title_tokens)
  PARTITION BY one_id,
  INTERLEAVE IN one
  OPTIONS (sort_order_sharding = true);
```

issue.title: Performance Degradation in Long-Running Spanner Emulator Sessions
issue.body:
I've been utilizing the Spanner Emulator for testing purposes within my environment, paired with PHPUnit. 
The feature set has been performing exceptionally well. 
However, I've noticed a significant slowdown during prolonged testing sessions. Specifically, the slowdown appears to coincide with the creation of new connections.

For reference, please see the related issue #72 and the reproduction project at https://github.com/kt81/spanner-emu-tester.

Below is an example of the performance degradation observed:

```
...
$ make run
13.6603ms
17.372299ms
31.821499ms
46.6992ms
55.764599ms
70.637199ms
83.588399ms
92.9404ms
107.0446ms
116.8905ms
128.591101ms
146.4209ms
153.661801ms
166.057102ms
...
```

This pattern suggests a gradual decrease in performance, particularly with an increase in the number of new connections over time. Any insights or suggestions on how to mitigate this issue would be greatly appreciated.

comments.body:
Here's a plot of 10k individual connections and query time of `SELECT count(1) FROM projects` in spanner emulator 1.5.18 on Windows.

![image](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/assets/192964/6ad13083-0729-480e-b670-6047b2dafe63)

If I do 128 clients concurrently (on a 32core machine), I get this density plot for the query times:

![image](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/assets/192964/6589873a-3ba8-4b4a-95e1-cb6fea57f9fb)

With multiplexed sessions they won't be cleaned up at all. It seems DeleteSession is a no op for them.

Even dropping the database doesn't seem to cleanup the related sessions, even though the comment in https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/ea685ac6a5c9cba6e346e88501933ee91a11f6cf/frontend/collections/session_manager.cc#L114 suggests they should.

Thank you for creating the reproduction project and providing the analysis! 🙏 

I have confirmed that a single loop is leaving 100 sessions open, which appears to be a bug in the Golang client. The large number of sessions then slows down the emulator lookup of the session within a map (which is `O(log(n))`).

> Emulator should cleanup the sessions automatically when a connection drops.

Unfortunately, the emulator doesn't track what connection made which sessions so the emulator cannot clean up the sessions when a connection drops. The sessions will be cleaned up after an hour of being unused.

> With multiplexed sessions they won't be cleaned up at all. It seems DeleteSession is a no op for them.

That is correct. Multiplexed sessions allow a client to only need a couple of sessions and remove the requirement to keep sessions alive meaning they aren't cleaned up for 28 days. The intention was to remove the need for session management in the client.

The emulator implementation has been written to match production but I think it needs to be reworked because the 28 day period likely isn't relevant for emulation. Unfortunately, it does also create issues for workflows that open and close clients frequently as the sessions will stack up (albeit, slower than the 100 session leak case).

My current recommendation would be to reuse the same client where possible and either use multiplexed sessions as it will create less sessions per client, or manually drop the sessions before closing the client.

I will continue to look into this and provide an update by the end of the week 👍

@larkee thanks for the update. It does feel like the performance drops as O(n) for some reason; the `select 1` measurements, also support that view. If it were O(log n), I think it wouldn't have such a large problem. Maybe there's something in the system that accidentally creates a linear lookup?

Our use case for spanner emulator is using it as a test backend. We ended up starting a new spanner emulator per test, which improved things significantly. Partly due to the session accumulation issue and partly due to the global locks.

This is caused by the following:
1. We have two images of the emulator; amd64 and arm64
2. In addition, we have a manifest file that contains a link to both images.
3. The two images and the manifest are not published at the exact same time.
4. This means that if you happen to do a `docker pull` right after the amd64 image has been built and published, but the arm64 image has not yet been published, then you will get the amd64 image even if your local machine is arm64.
5. If you then later do another `docker pull` after the arm64 image has been released, you will get that image.

We'll look into whether it's feasible to publish all three at the same time to avoid this confusion.

issue.title: Deleting a session with an active read/write transaction leaves the emulator in an invalid state
issue.body:
If you execute the following steps:
1. Create a session with name `session-1`
2. Start a read/write transaction on `session-1`
3. Execute at least one statement on the read/write transaction on `session-1`
4. Delete `session-1` while the transaction is still active
5. Trying to commit/rollback the transaction on `session-1` will fail with a `Transaction not found` error.
6. Trying to begin a new read/write transaction will fail with the error that the emulator only supports one simultaneous transaction.

The above steps will therefore leave the emulator in an invalid state, as it is impossible to end the non-existing transaction, and also impossible to start a new one.
